chunks: Al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abi 'Abdillah عليه السلام, who said:

There was a group who would drink and become intoxicated, then wound one another with knives that were with them. They were brought before Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام, and he imprisoned them. Two men among them died, and two men remained alive. The families of the two slain said: 'O Amir al-Mu'minin, exact retaliation from these two for our two companions.' So 'Ali عليه السلام said to the people: 'What do you think?' They said: 'We think that you should exact retaliation from them.' 'Ali عليه السلام said: 'Perhaps those two who died each killed his companion.' They said: 'We do not know.' So 'Ali عليه السلام said: 'Rather, I will place the blood-money of the two slain upon the tribes of all four, and I will take the compensation for the wounds of the two remaining from the blood-money of the two slain.'
And Isma'il ibn al-Hajjaj ibn Artat mentioned, from Simak ibn Harb, from 'Abd Allah ibn Abi al-Ja'd, who said: 'I was the fourth of them, and 'Ali عليه السلام gave this judgment concerning us.'

key_terms.دِيَةَ: blood-money or financial compensation for wrongful killing or injury
key_terms.قَبَائِلِ: tribes or clan groups bearing collective liability

ai.seo_question: How did Imam 'Ali عليه السلام rule in a case of mutual drunken violence when the killer could not be identified?
ai.summary: This hadith reports a judicial ruling of Amir al-Mu'minin 'Ali عليه السلام concerning a drunken violent altercation in which responsibility for the killings could not be determined with certainty. He did not impose retaliation without clear proof, but instead distributed liability through blood-money and compensation for injuries, reflecting caution and justice in criminal adjudication.
